title: Vowels
goal: Four thumb keys make every English vowel: A and O on the left, E and U on the right. Together they make the long ones.

blocks.x: Notice the short *i* is two keys, `EU`, because `E` alone is already the short *e*.
Long vowels and diphthongs: more keys
The vowel and its `R` often share keys (`UR`, `AR`, `OR`); lesson 6 covers those.
`*` sits in the vowel group but is not a vowel. It is a **tiebreaker**: when two words would take the same stroke, one gets the star. You will see it in lesson 9.
Two spellings of the same sound

A few vowel sounds take different keys depending on how the word is spelled. {{moon}} has `oo` and uses `AO`; {{tune}} has `u` and uses `AOU`. The rules read the spelling to pick, so you can too: spell it, then strike what you see.

blocks.q: Which keys make the vowel in {{bet}}?
blocks.why: Short e is the bare E key.
